units.function: Mocked HTTP tests for creating an OpenClaw-focused Agent invitation prompt by a same-Company CEO Agent or a board user with invite permission, plus branded invite-summary projection.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent-key or board-session actor identity enters an access route; Agent service role lookup or accessService permission decides authority, database stubs create an Agent-only invite, and Company/storage projections supply branding and onboarding links.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/board actor source and Company scope, Agent free-form role, users:invite-style permission decision, Agent-only Company invite/default agentMessage, bearer invite URL/onboarding text path and public Company branding.
units.lifecycle: Cross-Company and non-CEO Agents are rejected; a same-Company Agent whose role equals CEO creates an Agent-only invite and may attach a message. Board users require an explicit permission. The returned prompt references the public invite and onboarding document.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover cross-Company short-circuiting, negative/positive Agent role cases, positive/negative board permission and basic invite/branding response. Missing are accountable-human approval for Agent-created invites, role provenance and lifecycle, explicit Agent capability grants, rate/budget limits, inviter attribution, activity evidence, prompt injection, invite expiry/revocation, duplicate/idempotent creation, transactionality and proof that a CEO Agent cannot bootstrap uncontrolled Agents or delegate greater authority than it owns.
units.designRationale: Let a top-level Agent self-expand its workforce while retaining a conventional human permission path and same-Company guard.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS may let Agents propose hiring or Connector onboarding, but a real accountable human must authorize new Agent principals, roles, permissions, data access and reporting responsibility.
units.companyOsFit: Reject Agent-title-based invitation authority. An Agent may create a HireProposal containing capability requirements and evidence under its own bounded permission, but a qualified human accepts a ResponsibilityContract and ConnectorBinding digest before any credential or principal is issued. Board/human invitation authority must use IdentityPort principal and scoped policy, not a generic board abstraction.
units.responsibilityConflict: A same-Company Agent becomes an inviter solely because its free-form role is CEO; the created invite has no human approver and the stored inviter user is null. Free-form agentMessage enters an Agent-consumed onboarding flow. This permits an Agent to expand organizational authority without a legal/accountable human decision.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres tests for atomically claiming the first instance administrator and running additional initialization inside the winning database transaction.
units.dependencyDirection: An authenticated caller-supplied user ID enters a bootstrap service; the service writes instanceUserRoles and optionally invokes a transaction-scoped callback, returning claimed or already_claimed with the existing principal.
units.keyDataModels: User ID, instance_admin role, claimed/already_claimed status, existingUserId and generic onClaim transaction result.
units.lifecycle: The first sequential claimant inserts one instance-admin role and may perform related database initialization in the same transaction; later claimants receive the existing winner and no extra role row.
units.testAssessment: Real database coverage proves sequential uniqueness and callback visibility inside the winning transaction. Missing are simultaneous claims from separate connections/processes, callback failure rollback, retry/idempotency, invalid/deleted users, authenticated identity proof, endpoint exposure and CSRF, local-presence/bootstrap-token policy, audit event, timeout/deadlock and recovery when the first admin is lost.
units.designRationale: Provide a race-resistant zero-admin bootstrap while allowing membership or other initial state to commit atomically with the role.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted Company OS requires a secure first-owner ceremony that cannot be claimed remotely by an arbitrary early request and remains recoverable without hidden vendor control.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the single-winner database transaction and structured conflict result. Gate it behind an explicit uninitialized state plus local-console or one-time bootstrap proof, bind the claimed IdentityPort principal and deployment instance, log an immutable ceremony event, test true concurrency and callback rollback, then permanently disable the endpoint; define a separate audited recovery ceremony.
units.responsibilityConflict: The tested function trusts a supplied userId and proves no identity assurance or local presence. Returning an existing user ID may also disclose administrator identity. Without a bootstrap ceremony and audit evidence, first network arrival could become the ultimate authority.
